chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

A Bedouin from the clan of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) and said to him, 'Advise me.' Among what he advised him was: 'Endear yourself to the people, and they will love you.'

key_terms.أَعْرَابِيّ: A desert Arab / Bedouin — one from among the nomadic Arab tribes, distinct from urban Arabs
key_terms.بَنِي تَمِيمٍ: The clan of Banu Tamim — a major Arab tribe of the Arabian Peninsula
key_terms.تَحَبَّبْ: Endear yourself / actively show love — from the Form V verb تَحَبَّبَ, meaning to make oneself beloved or to demonstrate affection

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad advise a Bedouin who asked him for counsel? What is the Islamic teaching on earning people's love?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that a Bedouin from the tribe of Banu Tamim sought counsel from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), and the Prophet's key advice was to show love and kindness toward people — for this is the means by which one earns their love in return. The teaching reflects the Prophet's understanding that social bonds are built through active demonstration of affection, not merely through expectation of it. This counsel would have resonated deeply with Arab tribal culture, where loyalty and reciprocal bonds were the foundation of community life.
